willkommen.3: And we'd absolutely love for you to come party with us on the Croatian coast.
willkommen.4: We know Croatia isn't exactly around the corner – so we're super grateful to every single one of you making the trip. To keep things as easy as possible, we've put everything you need on here: where to stay, how to get there and what's happening on the day.
willkommen.5: Let us know by 1 May 2027 if you're in (RSVP).
willkommen.6: Can't wait to celebrate with you guys and make some memories!
story.3: That's the official name the family gave this little alliance: King Ivan and his Queen Nghi.
story.4: A one-of-a-kind mix of Croatian and Vietnamese roots – proudly “Made in Germany”.
story.5: Living proof that even a swipe to the right can be part of God's plan – guiding two hearts through a whole sea of options until they found their forever kingdom, built on faith, love and doing life together.
story.8: If you're wondering why this whole site says NGHIVAN when you probably know me as Minnie or Minh Nghi – here's the quick version for anyone who's not into Vietnamese naming rules:
story.9: In Vietnamese, the name you actually go by comes last. Nghi is my real first name and Minh is my middle name. Put Minh Nghi together with a bunch of kindergarten kids who couldn't pronounce it, and boom – Minnie was born!
story.11: Looks like a tongue twister, but it's actually easy: think of the word “singer”, swap the “er” for an “ee” – then drop the start and just say the back part:
story.17: Depends who you ask! Our parents were told we bumped into each other on a night out (which is true!).
story.18: What we left out: a little swipe to the right got the whole thing started. One first date later, the online match turned into a match for life.
story.19: What happens when one of us gets hungry?
story.21: Ivan can handle being hungry just fine – Nghi without food, on the other hand, is a full-on force of nature.
story.22: Ivan's survival hack: Always have an emergency snack on you, or at least know where the next one is. One bite – and peace is restored!
story.23: Who takes longer in the morning, and whose fault is it when we're late?
story.24: The official story: Ivan swears to everyone – and everyone happily believes him – that it's obviously always Nghi.
story.25: The truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth: It's Ivan. EVERY. SINGLE. TIME!
story.26: Nghi's standing at the door, shoes and jacket on, ready to go – and that's exactly when Ivan realises he urgently needs to go number two. And just like that, it looks like Nghi was the one running late. Smooth, Ivan. Real smooth.
story.28: Did Nghi see the proposal coming?
story.30: Not really! After the Vietnam trip – where Nghi was 100% sure he'd propose and nothing happened – her expectations for the last-minute Greece trip were at rock bottom. Only precaution: she still got her nails done before the flight, obviously (“You never know…”). 💅
story.32: Ivan had planned it for that weekend. While hunting for the “perfect spot”, he kept bombarding Nghi with weird questions, didn't listen to a single answer and drove her completely up the wall. On Sunday night, things properly blew up. It was so weird that Nghi was scared this would be the trip where they realise they just don't work as a couple!
story.34: After a romantic dinner, Ivan finally popped the question on their walk. Nghi was crying happy tears so loudly that she missed half of Ivan's speech. Ivan actually had to check whether she'd said “YES!” …
story.35: What does it mean to us that you're coming to our wedding?
story.37: We know it's a big deal to take the time off, make the trip to Croatia and spend the money & effort to be there with us. It honestly means the world to us.
story.38: And if you can't make it, we totally get it – you'll still be there with us in our hearts! To everyone coming: we can't wait to make some unforgettable memories with you. Love you all! ❤️
unterkunft.2: So nobody has to walk far after the party, here are your options for places to stay around our venue in Petrčane. Full-on hotel comfort with a sea view, or a cosy apartment or villa with friends & family – just pick whatever works for your plans and budget!
unterkunft.4: Staying at the hotel? Just enter our code on hotel-pinija.hr for 5 % off (sadly that's all we could get 😭).
unterkunft.11: If you want max comfort: stay right at the 4-star Hotel Pinija. You'll basically stumble straight from the dance floor into bed – and wake up to breakfast with a sea view.
unterkunft.18: Holiday rentals & Airbnbs <small>Right next door & cheaper</small>
unterkunft.19: Petrčane has loads of gorgeous private apartments, guesthouses and villas with pools – many right behind Hotel Pinija (just a 2–5 minute walk). Usually way cheaper and perfect for families or groups of friends.
unterkunft.21: How to find them: Just search “Petrčane” on Airbnb or Booking.com.
unterkunft.22: 💡 Want to team up? Keen to share an apartment or villa with other guests but don't know who's still looking? Just give us a shout – we'll happily connect you!
unterkunft.23: 🌊 Good to know about the beach: All beaches in Croatia are public! So even if you're not staying at the hotel, you can totally use the beach at Hotel Pinija. Just bring your own towels or beach mats (the hotel's sun loungers cost extra or are for hotel guests only).
unterkunft.29: Don't want to spend the whole time in Petrčane? The coastal towns around it are a great base too. Popular combo: 1–2 nights close to the action, then the rest of your trip in a cosy apartment or at a campsite in one of the quieter villages nearby.
unterkunft.30: Why the villages are perfect for a beach holiday: Zadar has a gorgeous old town and great restaurants, but the city beaches usually can't compete with the ones in the villages around it.
unterkunft.31: Our tip: Spend your days in the crystal-clear water out in the villages, then head into Zadar in the evening for a wander, some culture and dinner. More tips under Travel.
unterkunft.34: Want to stay together as a group, have a bit more freedom or stick around longer? Here are our favourite places nearby – just book directly on whatever site you like.
travel.flug.1: <small class="h3__pre">Closest airport:</small> Zadar International Airport <small>(ZAD) · 20 min to Hotel Pinija</small>
travel.flug.2: If you're coming from the Munich / Bavaria area: we've flown from Memmingen (FMM) to Zadar loads of times.
travel.flug.5: Midweek flights can be crazy cheap – with a bit of luck and just a small backpack/carry-on, you can get tickets from 35 € per flight.
travel.flug.8: There are cheap off-site car parks (about a 10–15 minute walk to the terminal) where 4–5 days only cost around 40 €.
travel.flug.9: Leave some buffer time at the barrier
travel.flug.10: Sometimes you'll have to wait a bit for a space to free up. Our trick: time your arrival at the car park with 1–2 flights landing before yours – that's exactly when people coming back are driving out.
travel.us.2: Good news if you're flying in from the States: United Airlines has a nonstop flight from Newark straight to Split!
travel.us.6: Getting from Split to Petrčane / Zadar
travel.us.7: From Split Airport it's about a 1.5-hour drive up the coast to Petrčane – and it's a gorgeous one. Renting a car right at the airport is super easy and the best way to get to the wedding, plus you're free to explore the coast!
travel.us.9: Or look for an easy 1-stop connection straight into Zadar Airport (ZAD) – it's only 20 minutes from Hotel Pinija.
travel.auto.7: ⛽ Fuel tip: Fill up first in Austria and then again in Croatia – fuel's usually a lot cheaper there.
travel.auto.9: Seriously, don't forget to buy your toll passes online before you leave! It saves you tons of time at the toll booths and keeps you clear of expensive fines.
travel.auto.12: Section tolls: Tunnel fees on the Tauern motorway (Tauern and Katschberg tunnels) plus the Karawanken tunnel heading south.
travel.auto.14: E-Vinjeta: Digital vignette for Slovenian motorways (1 week or 1 month, depending on how long you're staying).
travel.auto.15: Get it officially in advance from ASFINAG →
travel.auto.17: Just grab a ticket when you get on the motorway and pay when you get off (cash or card, easy).
travel.auto.18: ⚠️ Heads up for the drive home (Karawanken tunnel)
travel.auto.19: Driving home north through the Karawanken tunnel? The northbound tunnel toll is paid on the Slovenian side at the Hrušica toll station – not in advance through the Austrian ASFINAG.
travel.auto.22: We've done this drive more times than we can count, and we always make these two stops:
travel.auto.24: Start – about 9 hours to the coast.
travel.auto.26: Perfect for cheap fuel. There's a McDonald's right next to the JET petrol station for a quick snack. You have to come off the motorway for a bit, but it's worth it!
travel.auto.28: Petrol station – from here we take the country roads. Heads up, it's super windy – if you get carsick easily, bring some motion sickness tablets!
travel.auto.30: If you'd rather wait and fill up in Croatia, there's an INA petrol station right after the border (warning: TONS of mosquitoes!). Fuel at the motorway stations is definitely pricier.
travel.auto.32: You made it – straight into the sea! 🌊
anreise.3: We really recommend renting a car. Locals don't really use public transport much and it's hard to say how reliable it is (honestly, we've never used it there ourselves). With a car you're super flexible and can get anywhere easily!
anreise.6: Here are our top insider tips to make your trip to the Croatian coast perfect.
anreise.8: A must if you've never been! They protect your feet from sharp pebbles and sea urchins. You can even get ones that look like normal (white) sneakers. We got ours on Amazon.
anreise.10: A thin foldable foam mat or a padded beach mat makes lying on the pebbles way more comfy – a towel usually doesn't cut it.
anreise.12: Thanks to the pebble beaches, the water is crystal clear – you can see everything underwater!
anreise.14: Perfect if you like swimming, e.g. out to the Kornati islands or Dugi Otok. The boat stops in stunning bays so you can swim and snorkel right off the deck. We've only done one so far, but we'd totally recommend it. Hit us up for links (swimmers only).
anreise.16: Croatia uses the euro and cards work almost everywhere, but small beach bars, bakeries or parking meters sometimes only take cash.
anreise.18: The sun is no joke – and in the evening under the pine trees, bug spray is your best friend.
anreise.21: Zadar · Nin · Ražanac · Posedarje · Novigrad · Sukošan
anreise.23: Dugi Otok – 100% recommend booking a guided boat tour!
anreise.25: Vodice · Šibenik · Split · Makarska · Gradac · Drvenik (Brin)
anreise.29: 🎬 Game of Thrones filming locations Dubrovnik (King’s Landing) and Split (Daenerys’ dragon dungeon) are right on the coast.
anreise.30: 🏝️ Islands & boat trips Book a day trip by boat, or rent your own if you've got a boat licence.
anreise.31: 🍷 Wine & olive oil Chilled tastings at traditional konobas out in the countryside.
anreise.32: 🏛️ Culture & nights out Old-town wanders, restaurants and bars in Zadar (15 min) or Split.
anreise.33: Krka National Park Insane waterfalls and wooden boardwalks near Šibenik.
anreise.34: Trogir UNESCO-listed old town on a tiny island just before Split.
anreise.35: Primošten Super pretty fishing village on a peninsula with a lovely promenade.
anreise.36: Omiš Where the river meets the sea – steep cliffs, ziplining & rafting.
anreise.37: Hvar & Brač E.g. Bol / Zlatni Rat (Golden Horn) – by ferry from Split.
anreise.38: Ston & Mali Ston Europe's longest fortress wall & fresh oysters.
anreise.39: Kravica Waterfalls On the way to Mostar (BiH) – great for a swim.
bridal-party.3: Got questions or need anything? Our bridal party has your back. Don't know who's who yet? Just message our brothers – they'll happily put you in touch!
rsvp.2: Please let us know by 1 May 2027. Just type in your name – takes a minute, tops.
rsvp.4: Share photos with the Joy app
rsvp.5: Download Joy and join with our event handle. Check out photos, share your own and stay in the loop wherever you are.

meta.title: Minh Nghi & Ivan · 4 September 2027
meta.description: We're getting married! Minh Nghi & Ivan – Saturday, 4 September 2027 in Petrčane, Croatia. Everything you need to know about where to stay, getting here and RSVPing.
area.1.character: Petrčane's quiet next-door village, surrounded by lots of green. Pretty exclusive and super relaxed (rumour has it Luka Modrić has a house here).
area.1.perfect: Anyone after a quiet, private place to stay who still wants to be in Petrčane or Zadar in no time.
area.2.character: A green, upscale peninsula right next to Petrčane. Fancy resorts, gorgeous well-kept beaches and a beautifully lit seaside promenade.
area.2.perfect: Anyone who likes it a bit quieter, close to nature and a little chic – but still right near the action.
area.3.sub: Ivan's home village in the hills
area.3.character: A tiny, charming mountain village where Ivan's family comes from and his parents still live. Green hills and big mountains instead of sea views – but still only minutes from the quieter beaches on the coast.
area.3.perfect: Anyone who wants to see the real, rural Croatia, far away from the tourist crowds (perfect if you've got a rental car).
area.4.character: A real, slightly rougher-around-the-edges coastal town on the Velebit Channel with amazingly clear water and beautiful natural beaches. Still very unspoilt and laid-back.
area.4.perfect: Anyone after peace and quiet, nature lovers and anyone wanting to escape the crowds. Epic views of the Velebit mountains!
area.5.character: A lively but chilled coastal town with the huge Marina Dalmacija and kid-friendly pebble and sand beaches. Lots of Ivan's boys will be staying here too (after the wedding)!
area.5.perfect: Anyone who likes a social vibe. No big party strip, but nice beach bars and restaurants.
area.6.character: The historic port city and cultural hub of the region: Roman ruins, Venetian city walls, the Sea Organ and the “Greeting to the Sun” light installation.
area.6.perfect: Anyone into city life, sightseeing, tons of places to stay and actual things to do at night.
area.7.character: The heart of the wedding! A charming old fishing village with shady pine forests right by the pebble and rock beach, cosy taverns and amazing sea views.
area.7.perfect: Everyone who just wants to fall into bed after the party without having to drive anywhere.
area.8.character: Croatia's oldest royal town, sitting pretty on a little island in a shallow lagoon. Famous for the super long Queen's Beach and its healing mud.
area.8.perfect: Families with kids, sandy-beach fans and history buffs. Barely any nightlife – but proper holiday vibes.

infos.3: Everything you need to know for our big day – dress code, schedule and the questions everyone asks.
infos.dc.3: No strict rules – just wear whatever you feel good in and can party in!
infos.dc.5: Elegant, but with a breezy seaside feel: summery and festive, flowy fabrics welcome.
infos.dc.7: Soft, natural tones like sand, beige, pastels or ocean shades. You don't have to wear blue – just let the vibe inspire you.
infos.dc.9: As long as you're comfy and can party and dance with us all night long.
infos.plan.2: The full schedule is coming soon – we're still sorting out the last few details!
infos.faq.q1: Who do we ask if we have questions on the day?
infos.faq.a1: On the wedding day we'd rather not answer questions about the schedule – we just want to soak up every moment with you. For anything organisational, our maid of honour and best man, the bridal party, our brothers or Ana from Hotel Pinija are happy to help.
infos.faq.q2: Where can we park at the venue?
infos.faq.a2: Right in front of the venue. You can even drive onto the grounds and park in the shade under the pine trees – just a few steps from the party.
infos.faq.q3: How do we stay updated right before the wedding?
infos.faq.a3: Shortly before the wedding we'll set up a WhatsApp group. We'll share all the important updates, info and reminders with you there.
infos.faq.q4: What would you like as a gift?
infos.faq.a4: Honestly: we're not expecting gifts from anyone! Lots of you are travelling a long way and that's already expensive enough. You being there and celebrating with us is the best gift ever. If you'd still like to treat us to something, a little contribution to our honeymoon would be amazing.
infos.faq.q5: Do we need to say goodbye at the end of the night?
infos.faq.a5: Not at all! If you're running out of steam or want to head home while we're busy on the dance floor, feel free to just quietly slip out (a classic “Irish goodbye”). Don't worry about it at all – we just want you to have the best night and not feel like you have to come find us. We can't wait to see you again after the wedding and give you a proper hug then!
infos.faq.q6: Can we take photos during the ceremony?
infos.faq.a6: We're having an “Unplugged Ceremony”: our amazing photographers and videographers will capture every moment for all of us. So just be in the moment with us and keep your phones in your pockets – we can't wait to look out and see all your happy faces! If you spot someone pulling out their phone by accident, feel free to give them a friendly nudge.
infos.faq.q7: We're planning a surprise or a speech/performance – anything we should know?
infos.faq.a7: Love that! Please run any surprises or contributions past our Bridal Party first. If you don't have their contact, just message our brothers – they'll pass it on.
infos.faq.q8: What about the RSVP and food?
infos.faq.a8: Please make sure you RSVP by 1 May 2027 – no later. If you've got any dietary requirements or allergies you couldn't add in the RSVP form, just message us directly – nobody's going home hungry!
